# AGENTS.md

Instructions for coding agents (and humans) working in this repository.

## Language

- Repository content is in English: code, comments, docs, commit messages.
- Communicate with the owner in Russian.

## Ground rules

- No Flipper firmware forks. The FAP builds with stock `ufbt` pinned to
  firmware release 1.5.1 (`ufbt update --branch=1.5.1`, dotenv mode so the
  SDK lives in `flipper/.ufbt`; `flipper/.env` is git-ignored, each checkout
  creates it with `ufbt dotenv_create`). The Flipper must run 1.5.1.
- No hand-maintained Xcode project and no UI tests. The Mac host and all
  tests are a SwiftPM package built with `swift build` / `swift test`. The
  iPhone/iPad and Watch apps are thin shells in `host/Apple`, generated by
  XcodeGen from `project.yml` (the `.xcodeproj` and `Signing.xcconfig` are
  git-ignored) and built with `make apple-project apple-build`; CI never
  signs.
- TDD: write the failing test first, then the code. Every change ships with
  tests; all suites pass before moving on.
- Flipper hardware code (NFC, USB, BLE) stays behind small interfaces so that the
  rest of `flipper/src` compiles and is tested on the host with plain `cc`.
- The protocol fixtures in `protocol/fixtures/` are the contract: the C,
  Swift and Python test suites all run against them. Changing a message
  means changing the schema, the fixtures and both sides in one commit.
- Bambuddy internal inventory mode only; the host refuses Spoolman mode.
- The Flipper never creates an item without `material`.
- New host code paths log their outcome through `Log` (`FliBuddyCore/Logging`,
  see "Debugging" in `host/README.md`); secrets (the API key, the QR and
  sync payloads) never reach it.

## Layout

```
AGENTS.md, README.md
docs/superpowers/specs/   design docs
docs/design/              UI specs (Flipper, Mac) and the Flipper icon table
docs/plans/               implementation plans
protocol/                 PROTOCOL.md, JSON schema, fixtures (tag dumps,
                          sample messages) shared by all test suites
flipper/                  the FAP: application.fam, src/, images/
                          (generated XBM icons, see tools/README.md),
                          host-compiled unit tests in tests/
host/                     Swift package: FliBuddyCore library,
                          FliBuddyUI shared SwiftUI views,
                          FliBuddyMac SwiftUI executable, tests
host/Apple/               XcodeGen project.yml, iOS/ and Watch/ app shells,
                          Base.xcconfig, Signing.example.xcconfig
tools/                    Python dev bridge (Phase 0 spike, kept as a
                          debugging tool), fixture generators
.github/workflows/        path-filtered CI per part
```

## Test commands

```
make test                    # all three suites below
make -C flipper/tests test   # C unit tests, host-compiled
cd host && swift test        # Swift (FliBuddyCore)
cd tools && uv run pytest    # Python bridge, fixtures, schema
make lint                    # warnings fail: C -Werror, Swift, ruff
make coverage                # FliBuddyCore and tools line coverage >= 80 %
make apple-project apple-build  # iOS and watch apps for the simulators
```

`make test`, `make lint` and `make coverage` do not build the Apple apps.

## Environment notes

- If Xcode.app is installed but its license has not been accepted, `git`,
  `swift` and `cc` from `/usr/bin` fail with exit 69. Run them with
  `DEVELOPER_DIR=/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools` to use the Command Line
  Tools instead.
- The Command Line Tools have no XCTest; host tests use swift-testing. Its
  macro plugin needs the `-plugin-path` workaround that `host/Package.swift`
  applies when `DEVELOPER_DIR` is the Command Line Tools (see
  `host/README.md`).
- In `host/Sources/FliBuddyUI` and `FliBuddyMac` views use `@ViewState`, not `@State`: the
  SDK declares `@State` as a macro whose plugin only Xcode ships, so `@State`
  does not build with the Command Line Tools (see `host/README.md`).
- `make apple-project apple-build` needs XcodeGen and a licensed Xcode with
  the iOS and watchOS 26 SDKs; the Command Line Tools workaround above does
  not apply to them.
- Host tests give `SettingsStore` an `InMemoryKeyValueStore`, never
  `UserDefaults(suiteName:)`: `cfprefsd` rewrites a deleted suite's plist,
  so every test would leave one in `~/Library/Preferences`.
